text.p: Millicom International Cellular SA said Tuesday it will reorganize its business into four operating companies with continued financial and capital control at the parent level.
"We have decided to devolve operating responsibility to newly created regional operating companies rather than build up a centralized corporate orgnaization," the company said.
"This will place management closer to the operating companies and, in addition, provide an alternative level at which to finance these operations."
It said the four companies will be MIC Asia; MIC Latin America; MIC EEMEA, for Eastern Europe, Middle East and Africa; and MIC Systems.
MIC said the president of MIC Asia will be Roger Blott, currently the company's chief operating officer.
The company said the Latin American unit will be headed by its senior executive vice president - Latin America, Gustavo Prilick.
Peter Macnee, currently ssenior vice president operations, Asia, has been appointed president of MIC EEMEA.

And MiC Systems, which comprises MIC's 100 percent ownership of Multinational Automated Clearing House SA and its 50 percent interst in a Luxembourg service provider, will be headed by Michel Van Moer in addition to his present role as MACH president. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
